To: Myers, Gene <gmyers@freepress.com>
Subject: Re: UNNAMED SOURCES ... 
 
Got it, thank you.

Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: Myers, Gene
Sent: Wednesday, December 31, 2014 6:09 PM
To: Fenech, Anthony
Subject: UNNAMED SOURCES ... 
 
AF: An on-the-surface sentence like the one below is, officially, a violation of our policy of using unnamed sources. We cannot use phrases such as “an auto industry analyst” or “a veteran real estate agent” in stories. We must ID folks, or tell why we are not ID’ing them. This is especially important when an “unnamed” source criticizes someone or something. Saying Moya can hit righties but not lefties isn’t such harsh criticism – and it’s true – but it’s still criticism.
One longtime scout said at the MLB winter meetings last month that Moya could hit righties in the big leagues right now, but expected it would take a couple years to hit lefties.
Because I have heard this elsewhere – like from Price, for instance – here’s how you can get around the unnamed issue but still make the point:
There’s a view among at least some baseball people that Moya could hit righties in the big leagues right now, but will need a couple years to hit lefties.
Any questions? It’s good to learn on the job …
